summary: Length-prefixed (Pascal-style) strings, a small printf-like formatter and a line logger over a caller-provided byte array. In v1 lf_log_event hands an untrusted peer message to lf_format as the format string, so '%x' and '%s' in the message consume arguments that were never passed and leak stack or register contents or dereference junk pointers (uncontrolled format string, CWE-134); v2 renders the message through a constant '%s' format; v3 is a behaviour-preserving refactor of v2.

pairs.intent: CWE-134 fix: lf_log_event formats its message with the constant pstring "%s" instead of using the message as the format; the deprecated alias lf_log_msg is removed and lf_count_directives is added so callers can lint their own formats.

truth.label: changed
truth.notes: CWE-134: lf_format(line, sizeof line, msg) used attacker data as the format; v2 calls lf_format(line, sizeof line, plain, msg) with plain = "%s" (as a pstring).

pairs.intent: Behaviour-preserving refactor of v2: loop forms, renames, early return in place of if/else, switch case order, and the counter getters moved up next to lf_log_init.
